name: Assess asset condition and risk (annual health index update)
summary: Once a year asset analysts turn the inspection, test and failure records for poles, cables, transformers, switches, manholes and station equipment into a health index score for each asset, convert the scores into failure probability and risk, and rank renewal candidates for the pole, cable and station programs and the capital plan. Data comes from the station test database and the GIS mobile inspection tool, is copied by hand into Excel 'data loaders' per asset class, and the results are typed into the investment planning tool. The work is slow and error-prone because inspection records must be matched to GIS asset ids, test data is missing for many station assets, formulas live in spreadsheets, and odd results need a site visit to confirm.

baseline.org_archetype: A city-owned Ontario local distribution company serving about 346,000 customers with about 570 staff and an 80-person asset management and engineering division, modelled mainly on Hydro Ottawa.
baseline.notes: Reference period 2019 to 2022. In 2019 an outside consultant reviewed the ACA framework (initial assessment May 2019, follow-up October 2019) ahead of the 2021-2025 DSP.

unit_of_work: one annual asset condition assessment across 12 major asset classes
trigger: The year's distribution inspection, station maintenance and cable fault results are complete and the capital planning calendar calls for updated condition results.
end_state: Health index, condition demographics and ranked renewal lists are approved by the engineering manager and published to the capital plan and the pole, cable and station programs.

volume.seasonality: One update a year, run in late winter and spring after the field inspection season closes, so results are ready for the capital planning cycle.

evidence.note: Annual health index update feeding capital planning; 12 major asset classes reviewed by METSCO in 2019.

Seven asset engineers and analysts; about one and a half FTE across the year on data extraction, health index calculation, QA and ranking; the rest on capital planning, business cases and program support. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.
Kicks off the cycle and approves results. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.
Finds missing station test records and reviews station rankings. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

Reviews overhead and underground renewal rankings against field knowledge. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.
Fixes asset ids and attributes that do not match inspection records. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

systems.name: PowerDB substation test and maintenance database
Geographic information system (asset and network model)
Mobile workforce management and field tablets
ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Asset condition and health index analytics
Copperleaf C55 asset investment planning (AIP) software
Document management and engineering drawing repository

resources.name: Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Kick off the annual assessment
steps.description: The engineering manager confirms the data cut-off date, the asset classes and formula changes for the year (for example after the outside review's recommendations), and assigns asset classes to analysts with a due date tied to the capital planning calendar.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Extract station test and maintenance data
steps.description: An analyst exports transformer oil and dissolved gas results, insulation and breaker timing tests, tap changer and switchgear inspection results from the station test database for every station asset.

evidence.note: Station input data held in PowerDB and extracted manually (METSCO 2019).

steps.name: Extract distribution inspection and failure data
steps.description: Another analyst exports pole test and visual inspection results, padmount and vault inspections, infrared findings and cable test results from the GIS mobile inspection tool, and failure and outage cause records from the ERP and OMS.

evidence.note: Distribution inspection data from GIS Mobile Inspector; maintenance cycles revised since 2016.

steps.name: Reconcile inspection records with the asset register
steps.description: The analyst matches each inspection and test record to a GIS or ERP asset id, finds records for assets that were replaced or renumbered, and lists assets with no inspection in the cycle. Unmatched ids go to GIS for correction.

error.defect_description: Record matched to the wrong asset after a renumbering.

next.condition: gaps or unmatched ids to resolve

evidence.note: METSCO found data gaps per asset class and recommended targeted data collection.

steps.name: Request missing test results and id fixes
steps.description: The analyst emails the stations supervisor for missing test sheets and the GIS team for assets whose ids or attributes do not match, with a list and a deadline.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Stations supervisor supplies missing test sheets
steps.description: The stations supervisor looks for paper or PDF test sheets from contractors and crews, asks electricians about tests not yet entered, and sends what exists. Tests never done are flagged for next season's maintenance plan.

evidence.note: Six of eight station asset classes had health index sample sizes below 50% in 2019.

steps.name: GIS technician corrects asset ids and attributes
steps.description: A GIS technician checks each flagged asset against as-builts and work orders, corrects ids, install years and attributes, and confirms back to the analyst.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Load data into the class data loaders
steps.description: Analysts paste the matched data into the Excel data loader for each of the 12 asset classes (station transformers, tap changers, high- and medium-voltage switchgear, wood poles, overhead switches, overhead transformers, reclosers, cables, underground transformers, underground switches, manholes), refresh lookups and check row counts.

error.defect_description: Rows pasted out of alignment or a lookup range not extended, corrupting scores for part of a class.

evidence.note: Health index formulations and input data managed in a series of Excel data loaders; 12 classes reviewed in 2019.

steps.name: Calculate health indices and sample sizes
steps.description: The workbooks score each asset from weighted degradation factors (age, test results, visual condition, loading, failures) on a 0-100% scale, assign condition bands from very good to very poor, and report the share of each class with enough data to score. Station assets need at least 70% of inputs to get a score.

evidence.note: Weighted degradation factors, maturity levels and the 70% data rule for stations are described in the METSCO review.

steps.name: Check formulas and results
steps.description: A second analyst compares this year's scores with last year's by class, looks for assets that jumped bands without a new inspection, checks formulas and band thresholds, and sends errors back for correction.

control.basis: Asset management procedure: independent check of health index results

evidence.note: METSCO found calculation errors in the Excel workbooks; rework share estimated.

steps.name: Drive to sample sites with anomalous scores
steps.description: For a sample of assets whose scores look wrong (a new padmount scored very poor, an old station breaker scored very good) the analyst drives to the stations and street locations in a pool vehicle. Station visits are booked with the stations supervisor for access.

evidence.note: Field verification of a sample of anomalous health index results is common practice; frequency and time estimated.

steps.name: Inspect sample assets on site
steps.description: At each site the analyst, escorted in stations, looks at nameplates and visible condition, photographs the asset and compares it with the inspection record, then corrects the input or the score. Station entry follows the utility's work protection and site hazard rules.

control.basis: Station entry and hazard assessment under the Utility Work Protection Code and Occupational Health and Safety Act (Ontario Regulation 213/91 and utility rules)

evidence.note: Escorted station entry and pre-entry hazard assessment are standard utility safety rules.

steps.name: Convert scores to failure probability and risk
steps.description: For station assets the analyst converts each health index into a probability of failure with an industry curve and multiplies it by the customers and load at risk to get a risk cost per station. For distribution classes, failure rates by condition band are updated from the year's failures.

error.defect_description: Customer count or load at risk taken from an old station configuration.

evidence.note: Industry-derived HI-to-probability function and station risk cost described by METSCO.

steps.name: Produce condition demographics
steps.description: The analyst summarizes, by class, the share of assets past expected service life and in each condition band, and the change from last year, in tables and charts for the capital plan and, in filing years, the DSP.

evidence.note: 19% of assets past expected service life (51% of stations, 23% of overhead assets), 17% poor or very poor in the 2021-2025 DSP.

steps.name: Load results into the investment planning tool
steps.description: The analyst formats health index and risk results to the import template and uploads them to the investment planning tool against each asset, then spot-checks a sample of records after the import.

error.defect_description: Import maps results to the wrong asset or drops rows.

evidence.note: HI results uploaded separately into the C55 environment.

steps.name: Rank renewal candidates by program
steps.description: Analysts rank poles, cable sections, underground transformers and switchgear, and station assets by risk and condition, group them into practical work packages (by feeder, street or station) and size next year's program volumes.

evidence.note: Poor and very poor assets prioritized by risk; renewal programs by asset type.

steps.name: Field supervisors review the rankings
steps.description: Lines and stations supervisors go through the ranked lists in a meeting with the analysts, add assets they know are in worse shape, remove ones already replaced, and point out work packages that crews cannot reach or that clash with City works.

evidence.note: Common practice of reconciling analytic rankings with crew knowledge.

steps.name: Engineering manager approves results
steps.description: The engineering manager reviews the demographics, the main changes from last year and the ranked programs, asks for explanations of large swings, and approves the assessment or sends a class back.

control.basis: Asset management procedure: manager approval of condition results used for capital planning

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Outside consultant reviews the ACA framework
steps.description: Before a DSP filing the utility retains a consultant to review data processes, health index formulas, sample sizes and how results are used. The consultant issues an initial assessment, then a follow-up after changes; in 2019 the follow-up cost a fixed $17,000.

control.basis: OEB Chapter 5 filing requirements: description and support of the asset condition assessment in the DSP

evidence.note: METSCO engaged January 2019, initial assessment May 2019, follow-up October 2019, $17,000 fixed fee.

steps.name: Address review recommendations
steps.description: Analysts change formulas, data rules and documentation in response to the review, recalculate affected classes and record the changes for the DSP attachment.

evidence.note: Enhancements made between the May and October 2019 assessments.

steps.name: Publish the assessment
steps.description: The analyst files the ACA report and demographics in the document store and sends ranked renewal lists to the capital plan, the pole replacement program, stations maintenance and the inspection program (with assets lacking data for targeted inspection).

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

exceptions.name: Missing data and id mismatches
exceptions.description: Station test sheets and asset ids have to be chased before the data loaders can be filled.

exceptions.name: Spreadsheet calculation errors
exceptions.description: The checker finds loading or formula errors and the class is reloaded and recalculated.

exceptions.name: Field verification of anomalies
exceptions.description: Scores that look wrong are checked on site before results are used.

exceptions.name: Outside review of the framework
exceptions.description: Before a DSP filing a consultant reviews the framework and the team implements changes.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from kickoff to published assessment
benchmarks.population: Annual health index updates at a large Ontario LDC, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: two to four months between the end of the inspection season and the start of capital planning; years with an outside review run longer.

pain_points.description: Input data is exported by hand from the station test database and the GIS inspection tool into Excel data loaders, which loses data and introduces errors.

evidence.note: METSCO: manual extraction into stand-alone Excel files can result in data loss or errors.

pain_points.description: Health index formulas live in spreadsheets; calculation errors and inconsistent band definitions were found, and historical scores are not stored.

evidence.note: Calculation errors found; no process to store historical ACA data.

pain_points.description: Many station assets lack recent test data, so scores lean on age and sample sizes are low.

evidence.note: Six of eight station classes below 50% sample size.

pain_points.description: Results are typed or imported into the investment planning tool separately, so the ranking used in the capital plan can drift from the workbook.

evidence.note: HI results uploaded separately into C55; prioritization in Excel.

assumptions: The case starts on the annual calendar once inspection results are in; the triggers keep the organisation file's three inspection_findings sources, with shares reflecting where most records come from.
PowerDB and Copperleaf C55 are added as systems; the organisation file has only a generic asset analytics system.
Stations and lines supervisors and GIS technicians take part, though the organisation file's process map lists only asset analysts and the engineering manager.
An outside review of the framework is modelled in 5% of cycles: the model company commissioned one before the 2021-2025 filing, and the author assumes not every five-year term repeats it.
The field check uses a pool light vehicle; weather and station access windows are the waits that matter there.
Analyst FTE (1.0) is above the hands-on implied figure because analysts also spend time answering ACA questions in rate proceedings and maintaining the data loaders between cycles.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa 2021-2025 Custom IR Application, UPDATED Exhibit 1-1-8 Executive Summary (EB-2019-0261), May 5, 2020
sources.supports: DSP is the culmination of business strategy, customer engagement, capital investment, asset management and regional planning processes; 2021-2025 capital by OEB category averaging $100.8M net a year; forecast went through iterations for priority, customer preference, rate impacts, resource capacity and financing; 19% of assets past expected service life (51% of stations, 23% of overhead assets), 17% in poor or very poor condition; custom scorecard measures for stations and feeders exceeding planning capacity; nearly 21,000 customers took part in rate engagement.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa 2021-2025 Custom IR Application, UPDATED Exhibit 2 (rate base), including Exhibit 2-4-1 Capital Expenditure Summary (EB-2019-0261), May 5, 2020
sources.publisher: Hydro Ottawa Limited (OEB Regulatory Document Search)
sources.supports: Rationalization process: an engineering asset needs forecast first, then a review of asset needs, safety, reliability, growth, resource constraints, rate impacts, customer input and financing that cut the forecast by about $50M a year; top four drivers (customer service requests, failure risk, system capital investment support, capacity constraints); Cambrian MTS needed because South Nepean reached the limits of local transformation capacity, leave to construct applied for May 2019, approved October 2019, energization Q2 2022; System Renewal and System Service merged for tracking because funds shift between them; commitment to ISO 55000.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa interrogatory responses CCC-46 to CCC-79 (EB-2019-0261), including Attachments CCC-56(A) and CCC-60(A) and (B): METSCO review of Hydro Ottawa's Asset Condition Assessment framework (May and October 2019)
sources.publisher: Hydro Ottawa Limited (OEB Regulatory Document Search)
sources.supports: ACA input data held in PowerDB (substation tests) and GIS Mobile Inspector (distribution inspections), manually extracted into Excel 'data loaders' that calculate health indices; calculation errors found in the Excel files; health index results loaded into Copperleaf C55 for risk evaluation while investment prioritization was still done in Excel; HI converted to probability of failure and risk cost for station assets; 12 major asset classes reviewed (4 station, 4 overhead, 4 underground); station assets need at least 70% of data, six of eight station classes below 50% sample size; METSCO first engaged January 2019, initial assessment May 2019, follow-up October 2019 for a fixed $17,000; revised maintenance cycles (annual transformer visual and infrared, vault inspections every 3-6 years, annual XLPE cable testing).

sources.title: Filing Requirements for Electricity Distribution Rate Applications, 2021 Edition for 2022 Rate Applications, Chapter 5 Consolidated Distribution System Plan (June 24, 2021)
sources.supports: A DSP sets out asset management and capital expenditure plans over a minimum five-year forecast period plus five historical years; investments justified by reference to the asset management process; section 5.2.2 requires evidence of coordinated planning with the transmitter, IESO and regional planning deliverables; project or program justifications above the materiality threshold; asset condition assessment and prioritization methods described.

sources.title: An inside look at how Hydro Ottawa replaces electricity infrastructure
sources.supports: Condition is scored from visual inspections, electrical testing and infrared scans plus loading and location data into a health index; poor and very poor assets are prioritized by risk to reliability, safety and the environment; pole replacements on busy corners need City coordination to limit road closures and planned outages; underground cable work needs clear communication with customers whose property is crossed.
